conviction_note: Scaled number is (2*0.58-1)*19 = +3.0: the scale is the 18.7% event-implied move nudged up toward the name's 21.9% median reaction because a guide update is likely, and the lean is mild because the two FY26 beat-and-raises and benign Texas weather are inferences and proxies, set against a stock that has more than doubled off its April low with upside already paid in the skew. impact_sum (+2.7) and the scaled number agree in sign and size, and neither rests on a company number the market has not seen.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue (Porch-owned, ex-Reciprocal) consensus $133.4M (6 analysts, range $129.5-138.0M) and EPS $0.02 (range $0.01-0.03) per https://walnutinvest.com/stocks/prch/forecast. Benzinga agrees at $133.2M revenue and $0.02 EPS (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/PRCH/earnings-forecasts), so two sources agree. Company guide: FY26 revenue ex-Reciprocal $506-517M, gross profit $419-429M, adj. EBITDA ex-Reciprocal $119-125M (raised 2026-07-29, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001784535/000178453526000046/prch-20260729xexx991.htm). H1 revenue was $241.2M (Q1 $109.4M + Q2 $131.8M) and H1 EBITDA $58.8M, so the guide implies H2 revenue of $264.8-275.8M (about $132-138M a quarter) and H2 EBITDA of $60-66M. Consensus sits at the low end of what the guide implies. FY RWP target $600M, against $255M in H1.
positioning_check: Short interest about 17.3M shares, ~15.3% of shares outstanding, as of 2026-09-15 settlement (AltIndex, https://altindex.com/ticker/prch/short-interest). Equibles had 16.2M short, 12.3% of float, 8.4 days to cover at 2026-08-21 (https://equibles.com/stocks/prch/shortinterest). Benzinga shows 21.8% of float (https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/PRCH/sentiment). Against 1.51M average daily volume, 17M shares short is about 11 days to cover, which makes this a crowded short. Skew_25d is -6.29 vol points (calls bid over puts, 'upside paid'), put/call OI 0.69, ATM IV 99.8%, event-implied move 18.66%. Spot $17.59 is 5.4% under the 52-week high and 175% over the 52-week low. Run-up is +5.6% over 20 days and -5.4% over 5 days. Insiders sold under 10b5-1 plans at about $18 on 2026-10-20.

findings.finding: Porch beat and raised in both 2026 prints. Q2 Porch-owned revenue was $131.8M against a $121.6M consensus (+8%) and FY26 adj. EBITDA ex-Reciprocal went from $103-109M to $119-125M; Q1 also beat and raised. Management said policies written are ramping from about 59k in Q2 to more than 70k a quarter by year-end, and the $600M RWP target needs about $345M in H2 (about +25% YoY against Q3 2025's $137.5M). The Q3 revenue consensus of $133.4M sits at the low end of the $132-138M a quarter the guide implies, so a third beat and a raise toward or above $125M EBITDA is the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name has bought its beat-and-raises: +12.52% (2026-02-11), +17.93% (2026-04-28, Q1 beat-raise) and +16.02% (2026-07-29, Q2 beat-raise). Q3 2025 (2025-11-05) fell 33.4% despite revenue and EBITDA beats, on a GAAP EPS miss (-$0.10) driven by interest and a warrant fair-value loss.
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus is still at the low end of the guide-implied run-rate even though the company beat by 8% last quarter. If the street had priced a third beat-and-raise, Q3 revenue estimates would sit near or above $136M and the FY EBITDA bar above $125M. The upside call skew and the 175% rise off the low show that part of this is in the price, which is why it is sized at about a tenth of the implied move.
findings.independence: The guide ranges and H1 figures come from the 8-K exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001784535/000178453526000046/prch-20260729xexx991.htm). The policy ramp comes from the call (webull). The consensus comes from https://walnutinvest.com/stocks/prch/forecast. Analysts raised targets on 2026-09-25 (Cantor $20) and 2026-10-14 (B. Riley $24, Craig-Hallum $22), per the same Walnut page. All of this derives from company statements.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 was a light catastrophe quarter for the Reciprocal's Texas-heavy book. KCC (July) said 2026 severe-storm losses in Texas and the Southeast were running below normal, with activity shifted to the upper Midwest. Gallagher Re put 9M26 global insured cat losses at $92bn, the lowest since 2019, and no Texas hurricane landfall appears in Q3 (the season's first major hurricane, Isaias, hit Florida on Oct 9, after quarter-end). Q2 carried a $14M storm and a Reciprocal net loss of $19.8M, so a cleaner Q3 should mean surplus growth from the $169.9M Q2 level, which supports RWP growth under the 5:1 premium-to-surplus guardrail.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history isolates weather. The Q2 2026 print carried a $14M storm and still rose 16%, which suggests holders look through Reciprocal weather because adj. EBITDA ex-Reciprocal is mostly fee-based.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a regional weather proxy nobody aggregates for Porch. If it were priced, estimates for Reciprocal surplus or net income would exist, and they do not. But the line mostly sits outside Porch's ex-Reciprocal EBITDA, so its transmission to the stock is small.
findings.independence: Proxy. Gallagher Re's 9M26 report via Claims Journal (https://www.claimsjournal.com/news/national/2026/10/21/340831.htm, 2026-10-21) shows a quiet nine months. Against it: Allstate's Q3 2026 cat losses were $1.65bn, about 3x the year before (https://www.artemis.bm/news/allstate-reports-220m-september-pre-tax-cat-losses-taking-aggregate-year-to-3-37bn/), with half of August from a single wind and hail event in an unnamed region. That is likely the Midwest, but this is not confirmed.

findings.finding: Texas homeowners pricing is softening. The Texas Department of Insurance said on 2026-10-08 that most homeowners insurers filing since July 1 proposed decreases, averaging -4.3% across about 700,000 policyholders (ASI Lloyds -6%, Texas Farm Bureau -5.2%). On the Q2 call Porch said competitors cut prices in May and conversion stepped down before recovering in June, premium per new customer fell 4% and RWP per policy fell 16%. Porch's fee revenue is tied to written premium, so more competitor price cuts in Q3 threaten conversion or premium per policy.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 disclosed the May conversion dip and lower premium per policy, and the stock still rose 16.02%. Q3 2025, when RWP per policy was $2,884, fell 33.4%, but that drop was attributed to GAAP EPS.
findings.why_not_priced: The TDI release is a state regulator's note that the stock wire does not carry, and it came after Porch last spoke. If it were priced, Q3 RWP-per-policy or growth estimates would have come down, and the October target raises show the opposite. The TDI figure is an unweighted filer average and says nothing about Porch's own reciprocal.
findings.independence: Porch's own Q2 call commentary on May competitive cuts (https://www.webull.com/news/15364638842037248) points the same way. Shrunk for the crowded short (~15% of shares out).

findings.finding: The 2026-10-13 8-K announcing the ~$200M Allied Trust acquisition said Porch 'expects to file' an at-the-market program so that Porch or the Reciprocal can sell PRCH shares, including the Reciprocal's ~16.2M share stake, to add surplus. EDGAR shows no S-3 or 424B5 as of 2026-10-22, so the filing could come with the Q3 10-Q. The money buys growth capital for surplus behind policies written growing +38% and the Allied deal, so it funds visible demand; the near-term effect is supply on a ~115M-share float.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for an ATM. In June 2026 the Reciprocal sold 2.1M shares to Porch's captive for about $15M to move capital into surplus, and the next print rose 16%.
findings.why_not_priced: The intent was disclosed two weeks ago, so it is largely known. What is not known is the size and timing, which could land with the 10-Q. If it were fully priced, the stock would not be within 5.4% of its high with calls bid.
findings.independence: EDGAR filing list (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001784535&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40) shows no ATM filed yet. Same company document as the Allied finding below.

findings.finding: The Allied Trust deal (8-K 2026-10-13) came with 2027 targets, assuming a 1 Jan close: more than $900M RWP, more than 360k policies and more than $180M adj. EBITDA ex-Reciprocal, against a $119-125M FY26 guide, with Allied contributing about $25M. Q3 is the first call where management can defend or detail those numbers. The deal was announced before the print and its terms are public.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for M&A. The 20-day run-up of +5.6% includes the announcement window.
findings.why_not_priced: The numbers are public, so they are mostly priced. What remains is whether the call firms the >$180M figure, which implies about $155M organic, or hedges it.

findings.finding: Positioning: about 15% of shares outstanding (12-22% of float, depending on source) is short, with roughly 8-11 days to cover, and the option market pays up for calls (skew -6.29). A beat-and-raise meets a crowded short that is underwater after the move from about $7 in April to $17.59.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 6 of 7 prior prints rose, three of them more than 20%. The one drop was -33.4%.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is public and so is the skew. Only the squeeze mechanics on a beat are not fully priced. Sized small.
findings.independence: https://equibles.com/stocks/prch/shortinterest (8.4 DTC, 2026-08-21). The baseline skew is independent of the short data.

findings.finding: Q3 2025's -33% reaction followed a GAAP EPS miss that included a $5.7M loss on the private-warrant fair value as the stock rose. The Q2 2026 income statement shows no private-warrant line any more (derivatives were +$0.86M), so a rising share price in Q3 2026 no longer produces that mark-to-market loss. Interest expense is still about $14.8M a quarter against an EPS bar of $0.02.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-11-05: -33.4% on GAAP EPS of -$0.10 against a positive consensus, despite revenue and EBITDA beats.
findings.why_not_priced: This is in the filings, but the EPS consensus range ($0.01-0.03) is narrow. A clean below-the-line quarter mainly removes the risk that sank last year's Q3 print rather than adding upside.
findings.independence: The Q3 2025 8-K exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1784535/000178453525000102/prch-20251105xexx991.htm) shows the -$5,702k warrant line. Both are company documents.

findings.finding: COO Matthew Neagle sold 31,250 shares at $18.01 and director Amanda Reierson sold 7,418 shares at $17.98 on 2026-10-20, both under 10b5-1 plans adopted 2026-06-15. Earlier Form 144s and Form 4s were filed in September and October.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The CEO's sell-to-cover sales in April and May 2026 came before a +17.9% print.
findings.why_not_priced: These are scheduled plan sales that carry almost no information, and they are already public.

findings.finding: NAR: September 2026 existing-home sales in the South were -0.5% YoY (national -2.2% YoY, 3.99M SAAR), so the home-transaction lead flow behind Porch's new-policy growth was flat rather than growing in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Porch grew policies written +38% in Q2 through a similarly weak housing market, so the stock has not traded on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a public macro series and is priced. Porch's growth is share gain, not market volume.

outside_window.finding: The Allied Trust closing is subject to Texas Department of Insurance approval and is expected in Q1 2027. Formal 2027 guidance comes after the close.

baseline_tension: The lean agrees with the upside-paid skew, the name's habit of rising on prints (6 of 7) and the crowded short, so it is partly priced. That is why p_up is only 58 rather than the 65+ a third beat-and-raise would justify on fundamentals, and it is held down further by the 175% run off the low and last Q3's -33% shock.
lessons_applied: Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the ATM buys reciprocal surplus for visible policy growth (+38%) and the Allied deal, so it went from -1.0 to 0.0, with the downside kept in the range.
Lesson 7 (crowded short, ~15% short, ~11 DTC): the Texas pricing negative was shrunk from -1.5 to -0.8, also as a proxy under lesson 5. Insider and housing negatives went from -0.2 to -0.1 each.
Lesson 5 (weather is a proxy; Porch's ex-Reciprocal EBITDA is fee-based): the weather positive went from +1.0 to +0.7.
Lesson 2 (one-off below operating income): the warrant-line finding went from +0.3 to +0.2.

Lesson 1 and 6: the bar is sourced to two agreeing estimates plus the company guide. The beat-and-raise finding stays at +2.0 because this name has bought its 2026 beat-and-raises; p_up moved from 57 to 58 only because the shrunken negatives no longer pull it down.
